workload.command: docker run --rm --init --stop-timeout 10 --name perfproof-rails-rails-pr58964-workload -e BUNDLE_WITHOUT=rubocop:mdl:doc:job:cable:storage -v .:/src -v perfproof-gems:/usr/local/bundle -w /src/activesupport perfproof-ruby-4.0-tzdata-legacy bundle exec ruby --yjit -Ilib -e "require 'active_support'; s = Object.new; def s.emit(event) = nil; r = ActiveSupport::EventReporter.new(s); 300_000.times { |i| r.notify('eval.event', id: i, name: 'x', ok: true, n: 3) }"
workload.source: written here from the description of https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/58964 (EventReporter#notify on every structured event, measured there under YJIT): 300,000 notify calls with a four-key payload to one subscriber

oracle.command: docker run --rm --init --stop-timeout 10 --name perfproof-rails-rails-pr58964-oracle -e BUNDLE_WITHOUT=rubocop:mdl:doc:job:cable:storage -v .:/src -v perfproof-gems:/usr/local/bundle -w /src/activesupport perfproof-ruby-4.0-tzdata-legacy bundle exec ruby -Itest -e "require './test/event_reporter_test'; require './test/event_reporter/log_subscriber_test'"
oracle.source: Active Support's EventReporter and its LogSubscriber tests (the latter changed by https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/58964); targeted tests only

evidence.note: description, as matched by the miner: speedup claims: 30% fewer

status_reason: built here and ran workload and oracle on the task and reference trees; see runs. Ruby is not installed here, so it runs under Docker (a linux/arm64 VM on this Mac) in the official ruby:4.0 image plus tzdata-legacy (eval/tasks/workloads/_images/ruby-4.0-tzdata-legacy/Dockerfile): Debian trixie keeps the legacy US/* zone names Active Support's tests use in that package. Gems are the tree's Gemfile.lock (bundler 4.0.12), without the rubocop, mdl, doc, job, cable and storage groups
